content.title: Costco slapped with fresh ‘automatic renewal’ lawsuit after 60-day notice ‘fail’
content.text: WAREHOUSE giant Costco is facing a new class action lawsuit from a customer angry about the retailer’s automatic membership renewal practices. The shopper alleged that the grocery company broke the law with its untimely and deficient membership renewal notices Sign up for the Money newsletter Thank you! Costco Wholesale operates an international chain of membership warehouses, carrying brand name merchandise at substantially lower pricesCredit: Getty Costco has been sued by an unhappy customer regarding its membership renewal practicesCredit: Getty Member Russel George sued Costco, claiming that the chain sends its shoppers an email notice 60 days before automatically charging them for membership renewals. In his class action lawsuit, George argued that Costco’s notices were untimely and fall outside the 45-day period outlined in California’s Automatic Renewal Law. “Due to Costco’s untimely and deficient auto-renewal notice, the plaintiff was deprived of information he was statutorily entitled to that would have notified him of the upcoming auto-renewal and provided him with methods of cancellation,” stated the lawsuit. The Costco shopper also alleged that the warehouse club’s membership renewal notices did not include certain mandated information, including the renewal length and terms, how much would be charged, and ways to cancel the automatic renewal. George argued in the lawsuit that he was surprised to find out the retailer had automatically renewed his Gold Star annual membership in January, charging $65 to his credit card. The charge came after the customer had been debating canceling his membership because he did not shop at Costco all too often. “Had the plaintiff been provided this notice in a timely manner, he would have canceled his membership and not gone forward with the auto-renewal,” stated the class action lawsuit. George claimed that the retailer had breached several laws, including California’s Automatic Renewal Law, False Advertising Law, Consumers Legal Remedies Act, and Unfair Competition Law. Most read in Money He has demanded a jury trial and requested declaratory and injunctive relief. George is also seeking an award of damages for himself and all class members. Costco membership sharing guidelines Costco has strict rules for membership use that shoppers must follow and they've been cracking down on offenders in recent years. Primary Member Use: Only the primary cardholder can use this Costco membership card. Sharing it for purchases is not allowed as the photo on the card must match the person using it. Household Card: Each primary member can add one free household cardholder who lives at the same address. This person will receive their own membership card and can shop at Costco independently. Guest Policy: Members can bring up to two guests per visit to Costco. However, only the member can make purchases. Guests must be accompanied by the member. Authorized Cardholder: For an additional fee, you can add an authorized cardholder, such as a family member or friend, who doesn’t reside at your address. They will receive their own card and can shop independently. Credit: Costco The U.S. Sun reached out to Costco for comment but did not hear back immediately. The retail giant has faced other legal trouble recently, hit with a class action lawsuit in February claiming that Costco sold rotisserie chickens contaminated with Salmonella. Another proposed class action lawsuit alleged that Costco wrongfully charged shoppers higher prices tied to federal tariffs before the Supreme Court ruled the duties imposed by the Trump administration as unlawful. Costco has confirmed it will refund customers if the government is forced to repay the costs incurred from tariffs. Story idea?
